goals.0: The German names of the 26 letters, plus ä, ö, ü, ß
grammar.0.title: The 26 letter names
grammar.0.intro: Tap each letter to hear its name. The hint underneath is the sound in Bangla.
grammar.1.title: The special letters
grammar.1.intro: These do not exist in Bangla — tap, listen, then say them yourself.
grammar.1.note: No special keys? You can write ae, oe, ue, ss instead.
grammar.2.title: The spelling alphabet (Buchstabiertafel)
grammar.2.intro: On the phone people spell names like this: “B wie Berta”.
grammar.2.note: You do not have to memorise them all — learn the words for the letters of your own name.
grammar.3.title: If you know English, watch these
grammar.3.text: E = “ay”, I = “ee”, J = “yot”, G = “gay”, V = “fow”, W = “vay”, Y = “ewp-si-lon”, Z = “tset”. These differ from the English names, so practise spelling at least your own name correctly in German.
quiz.0.why: The German name of W is “Weh” (vay).
quiz.2.prompt: What is the German name of the letter V?
quiz.3.prompt: Which one is a special German letter?
quiz.4.why: ü = say “ee” with rounded lips: Tschüss.
quiz.6.prompt: Put the words in order: “How do you write that?”
quiz.6.why: Question word Wie first, then schreibt.
quiz.7.why: Wie schreibt man das? = How do you write that?
